plans:
Heads-up: in plan mode every read tool is blocked, so I could not open CLAUDE.md or any project file yet. The plan below is therefore about *how* I'll check, not findings — I won't guess at what's wrong.

1. Read CLAUDE.md in full and turn each rule into a concrete checklist item (naming, formatting, file layout, allowed dependencies, test expectations, commit/scope rules, etc.).
2. Inventory the repo: list all tracked/modified files (including anything to be committed) and note tech stack, test command, and lint/format config.
3. Go through the codebase rule by rule and record every violation with file path + line number, so the fix list is verifiable rather than impressionistic.
4. Fix violations one at a time, reading each file before editing it and staying minimal — no opportunistic refactors, no behavior changes beyond what a rule requires.
5. Verify: run the test suite and any lint/format/typecheck script, and read back each edited file to confirm it matches the rule.
6. Report a short two-column table — "what was wrong" (with location) vs "what I changed" — plus a note on anything I could not verify or chose not to touch.

Two things I'll flag rather than silently decide:
- If a rule is ambiguous or conflicts with existing code, I'll pick the reading closest to the rule's obvious intent and call it out in the report instead of rewriting large areas.
- If a violation looks deliberate (e.g. a generated file, vendored code, or a documented exception), I'll mention it and leave it alone.

Please approve and I'll start with step 1.
